newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures down, but off lows on US data.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures down, but off lows on US data.

text.p: IMM currency futures fell, but traded off daily lows after U.S. economic data lent credence to ideas that the U.S. Federal Reserve may not raise U.S. rates in July, traders and analysts said.
"The dollar seems to go down if there are perceptions of no rate hike," one currency futures analyst said.
U.S. May retail sales, coupled with U.S. weekly jobless claims, suggested a slower pace of U.S. economic activity in the second quarter and immediately rallied U.S. T-bonds.
Sales fell 0.1 percent overall and excluding autos, versus estimates for up 0.4 percent and 0.3 percent, respectively.

In addition, April retail sales numbers were downwardly revised to down 0.9 percent overall for its biggest drop since February 1995 when sales fell 1.6 percent. April sales excluding autos were revised down 0.5 percent.
Meanwhile, U.S. jobless claims for the week ended June 7 rose to 339,000, against average trade estimates of 326,000 and the prior week's upwardly revised 338,000.

September yen cut their substantial losses after the data were released. Currency futures traders said the contract may find further direction from U.S. deputy Treasury secretary Lawrence Summers, who speaks this afternoon.
Summers is scheduled to speak at 1245 EDT/1645 GMT to the Computing Technology Industry Association conference in Washington D.C.
Most traders and analysts attributed yen futures' rally on Wednesday to Summers' comments that Japan should foster a demand-led recovery and avoid running up external surpluses.
However, the yen rally was overextended, as witnessed by the September yen's selloff overnight, several currency analysts said.
"You have a market that was stretched on short dollars," Dave Durrant, senior currency analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc, said.
Some analysts said the scramble for dollars started before comments from a former Ministry of Finance official.

Tomomitsu Oba, former ministry of finance (MOF) vice finance minister for international affairs, said current MOF official Eisuke Sakakibara has in mind a yen rate slightly stronger than 120 yen to the dollar.
The 120.00 spot yen level corrsponds to a September yen level of $0.008452.

At 0826 CDT/1326 GMT September yen was off $0.000237 at $0.008892, marks lost $0.0024 at $0.5846, Swiss francs were $0.0031 lower at $0.7010, sterling was $0.0022 lower at $1.6320, Canadian dollars were up $0.0014 at $0.7272, Australian dollars were $0.0043 lower at $0.7534 and Mexican pesos were $0.000100 higher at $0.120625.
